statement.essentials: The lower outer part of the gland is the largest of the five.
statement.anatomy: By weight the lower outer part (level II) is the heaviest level of the gland, followed by levels I and III, which are similar; the upper inner part (level IV) is the lightest of the four body levels.
statement.clinical: In 19 dissected glands level II made up 41–47% of the weight, levels I and III 20–22% each, level IV 8–10%, and level V, when present, under 5%.

limitations: Weights of one study of 19 specimens; the ranges depend on whether level V was present. The levels in the model are cut by the project’s own boundaries, and its volume shares differ from these figures (reported in the QC log, not tuned).
